label: paragraph_title
text: First Commander of Expeditionary

label: text
text: Following a sudden relapse, which came as a surprise and a shock to all, the death has occurred in England of Lord French, Earl of Ypres who was first Commander-in-Chief of the British Expeditionary Force in France and Viceroy of Ireland during the most troublous time in that country.

label: text
text: Force.

label: paragraph_title
text: FINAL BULLETINS.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: A bulletin states that the Earl of Ypres spent a fairly comfortable night. His condition this morning was much about the same but he was weaker.

label: text
text: Viscount French has held many posts, one around which much controversy has raged. This was the commandership of the British Expeditionary Forces in France in 1914 and 1915 from which he retired in favour of Sir Douglas Hodge after the disastrous battle of Loos.

label: vision_footnote
text: WORD FRIENCH FAZZI O ITTEN

label: text
text: Viscount French published a justification of his war record in 1919 dealing particularly with incidents during the retreat from Mons which had led to his proposal to abandon the French and land troops in Belgium and the question of shell shortage which involved him in a controversy with Mr. Asquith. "[Sir George Arthur's "Life of Lord Kitchener" also throws light on the matters in dispute.]

label: text
text: A great stir was caused by the attempt made on Vistount French's life on December 19, 1919, while he was acting as Viceroy of Ireland, a post to which he had been appointed owing to the troubled conditions in that country.

label: text
text: During the King's visit to the Front in December, 1914 he conferred the Order of Merit upon the Field Marshal and the next year he was the recipient of France's highest military honour, the Medaille Militaire. On relia-quishing command in December, 1915 he was created Viscount French of Ypres and on his return home became Commander-in-Chief of the Home Forces.

label: text
text: His period of association with Ireland as its Viceroy was not the only one during which his name was intimately connected with the country for he was one of the military leaders who tendered their resignations in March, 1914 in connection with the threatened movements of troops from the South following Lord Carson's threat regarding arms running.

label: text
text: His early career centred chiefly round South Africa and his name is immemorially associated with

label: text
text: the. relief of. Kimberley of February 15, 1900, and the Battle of Diamond, Hill in which he bore the brunt of the whole Boer attack.

label: text
text: He was appointed to command in South Transvaal in November, 1900 and on his return to England the next year he was given the command of the first Army. Corps at Aldershot, his next steps up to the appointment as Field-Marshal

label: text
text: of Forces (1907-11) and Chief of Imperial General Staff (1911-14). Prior to his career in South Africa, French did good work in connection with the Nile Expedition being present at Abu Klea, Gabul and Metarmneh. He also commanded cavalry with Sir George White's force in Natal. He was born at Ripple, Kent, in 1852, the navy being looked upon by his parents as his future sphere. He in fact served in the Navy from 1866-70 and did not enter the Army until 1874.

label: paragraph_title
text: SILK DUTIES.

label: text
text: THE DRAWBACK RATES ANNOUNCED.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: The following are the drawback rates on silk articles produced in Great Britain and North Ireland from material on which customs or excise duty are paid.

label: text
text: Silk in an article of soil yarn 17d, per lb, throwa yarn undischarged 45d, per lb, thrown yarn and spain yarn wholly or partly discharged 49d, per lb, tissue undischarged 51d, per lb, wholly or partly discharged if proved to the satisfaction of the commissioners to have been produced from imported undischarged tissue, 93d, per lb, soil tissue, made from imported nails 19d, per lb, any other case 66d, per lb.

label: text
text:
Doubled or twisted thread advanced beyond the stage of singles yarn 19d, per lb, tissue made from staple fibre or other waste, 11d, per lb, tissues proved to the satisfaction of the commissioners to have been made from other forms of artificial silk 21d.
In the case of articles made wholly or partly of silk or artificial silk which are proved to the satisfaction of the commissioners to have been charged duty and which are shown to be in such form and state that if duty had not been paid they would have been liable for life same rate of duty as already charged, then the drawback will equal the duty paid.
In the case of made up articles consisting wholly or partly of silk or artificial silk; if exported in the form and state in which imported, then the drawback will equal the amount of duty paid, and if manufactured in Great Britain or North Ireland from silk or artificial silk the drawback will equal the amount payable as drawback in respect of such quantity like silk or artificial silk as the commissioners opine has been used in the manufacture of the article.

label: paragraph_title
text: GREAT FLIGHT TO THE NORTH POLE.

label: text
text: AMUNDSEN STARTS:

label: text
text: FORTY-EIGHT HOURS' FLYING.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: : Oslo, May 22.

label: text
text: It is reported that Captain Amundsen, the famous Norwegian explorer who discovered the

label: vision_footnote
text: RAOLD AMUNDSEN

label: text
text: South Pole, started at 5.15 p.m. yesterday. from King's Bay for the North Pole, which he is expected to reach at midnight if all goes well.

label: text
text:
The flying will be ended within forty-eight hours from the start. The machines are carrying 2,400 kilograms of benzine and provisions for thirty days.
In the event of the necessity to return on foot, the ships "Hobby" and "Farm" are going as far North as the ice permits and will keep a lookout for the aviators.

label: text
text: A communique fronç. Fez states that General Chambrun carried out a brilliant operation in the centre enabling him to relieve the

label: paragraph_title
text: Abdel Krim.

label: text
text: Upper Werga district in spite of the furious enemy attacks with large forces hurriedly rushed up and the desperate resistance of others firmly entrenched in positions.

label: text
text: The artillery and air force gave valuable assistance to the French advance. The enemy's losses were considerable and the French casualties comparatively slight.

label: text
text: “Le Mabin's” correspondent in Madrid says that the ex-Minister, M. Malvy has completed his special mission to Spain. In the course of conversation he said that he was very satisfied with the results.

label: text
text: It is learned that the conversations between M. Malvy and General Primo de Rivera resulted in a Franco-Spanish agreement regarding Moroccan problems giving each freedom to carry out its plans. Referring to a possible collaboration between the French and Spanish fleets "Le Matin" thinks a big landing on the beach at Ajdir is more likely than the bombardment of Ajdir which is Abdel Krim's headquarters and the meeting place of international smugglers supplying the rebels with arms and munitions. It is impossible to bombard Ajdir because it contains thousands of Spanish prisoners.

text: It is reported from Tangier that some of the Moroccan tribes are reported to be ready to make a truce with Spain. A representative of Abdel Krim is expected to go to Tauri. Shortly to meet a

label: paragraph_title
text: UNEMPLOYMENT BILL REJECTED.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: paragraph_title
text: LONDON, May 22.

label: text
text: The House of Commons rejected by 216 to 118 votes the second reading of the Prevention of Unemployment Bill introduced by the Labour Party providing for the establishment of a national employment and development board with a State grant of £10,000,000 a year, the board to consist of Ministers of the Crown and to be empowered to make advances to dominion or colonial governments, local and public authorities to be spent anywhere in the Empire for purposes calculated to provide employment.

label: text
text: Mr. Lloyd George declared that nothing could be done under that Bill which the Cabinet was not able to do without it.

label: text
text: A Conservative motion for the rejection of the Bill declared the Bill afforded no real solution of unemployment and would further handicap industrial revival by placing a new burden on taxpayers.

label: text
text: At that time he somewhat ostentatiously displayed a wealth of bank notes, and said his misfortunes were due to the "machinations of the Minister of Foreign Power. Anyhow, back he went to America, and on this visit he succeeded in securing the daughter of a Kentucky millionaire as a bride, a romantic attachment which was shattered when the "Emir" was recognised as a tailor's presser in Chicago. Romance was blighted, and the hard-hearted American immigration officers saw that he was deported. Even then, he did not accept defens. He paid for an expensive suite aboard the liner he was forced to travel by, but not even the majesty of his title or his resplendent attire could serve him as an open sesame to this country.

label: text
text: The next move is with the American immigrant authorities, but whether they give him another trip to Liverpool or any other port on the face of the globe, it is unlikely that the last has been heard of this interesting character.
